daily_brief: Wildfires across southwestern France and central Spain have forced the evacuation of more than 220,000 people, prompting France to activate the EU's civil protection mechanism and Spain to declare a national emergency [BBC World, France 24, RFI English]. In Ukraine, Russian ballistic missile strikes killed at least 10 people at a drone technology exhibition near Kyiv, with President Zelensky warning of additional massive strikes within 48 hours [BBC World]. The International Criminal Court voted to remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual misconduct allegations, a decision he has vowed to challenge [BBC Europe, Le Monde]. Tensions between the US and EU escalated as President Trump threatened new tariffs and announced a Section 301 investigation in response to European fines on American tech companies [BBC Europe]. Meanwhile, the US-Iran conflict continued for a 13th consecutive night, with both sides signaling potential escalation as oil prices exceeded $100 per barrel [Globe and Mail]. Diplomatic developments included UN Secretary-General Guterres arriving in Syria for the first such visit since before the civil war began [France 24].

top_stories.headline: Wildfires Force Over 220,000 Evacuations Across France and Spain as Blazes Rage Out of Control
bullets: More than 200,000 people evacuated in France's Gironde and Landes regions near Bordeaux, with an additional 25,000 evacuated in central Spain and 40,000 told to shelter in place
Spanish officials describe the Madrid-area fire as 'beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain' after three fires merged into a single blaze
France activated the EU civil protection mechanism, receiving aircraft support from Croatia, Portugal, Czech Republic, and Slovakia; Spain declared a national emergency
French Prime Minister stated fires have reached 'a level that has never been seen before'; Madrid's regional president called it the 'worst fire in the history of the region'

top_stories.headline: Russian Ballistic Missiles Strike Drone Exhibition Near Kyiv, Killing At Least 10
bullets: Russian ballistic missile strikes hit an exhibition showcasing drone technology near Kyiv, killing 10 people and injuring approximately 100
Five additional people killed by Russian glide bombs in Sloviansk; two men killed in Sumy, bringing total Ukrainian deaths to at least 15
President Zelensky warned of intelligence indicating Russia is preparing another massive missile strike within 48 hours
Ukraine conducted retaliatory strikes killing six people in the Russian city of Kirov and targeting Wildberries retail warehouses

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage of casualties on both sides, noted prominent defence figures were safe

top_stories.headline: ICC Votes to Remove Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan Over Sexual Misconduct Findings
bullets: Assembly of States Parties voted 82 in favor to dismiss Khan as ICC chief prosecutor following misconduct investigation
Court oversight body found Khan committed 'serious breach of duty' by engaging in improper sexual relationship with junior staff member and attempting to suppress her complaint
Khan, elected as ICC's third prosecutor in 2021, was suspended last month; his lawyer said he will challenge the decision through 'all available legal mechanisms'
Decision comes amid unprecedented pressure on the court and could reshape the world's only permanent war crimes tribunal

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Detailed the institutional implications and noted Khan's denial of allegations

top_stories.headline: Trump Threatens EU Tariffs and Section 301 Investigation Over Tech Company Fines
bullets: President Trump announced US will launch Section 301 trade investigation into EU over fines imposed on Google, Apple, Meta, and Amazon
Threat follows EU's €890 million fine on Google this week; Trump demanded all fines be 'entirely reversed'
Trump stated he is considering 'substantial TARIFF' in addition to investigation
Announcement came one day after Trump imposed new tariffs of 10-12.5% on 60 trading partners including the EU, UK, and China

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Straightforward coverage explaining Section 301 powers and tariff context

top_stories.headline: US-Iran Conflict Enters 13th Night with Both Sides Signaling Potential Escalation
bullets: US military disabled merchant vessel M/T Lavine in Gulf of Oman after it attempted to breach American blockade of Iranian ports four times
Both sides indicated possible escalation: US embassies warned Americans departure options may become limited; Iran's Revolutionary Guard advised regional residents to avoid US bases
Saudi Arabia struck Yemen's Hodeida port in response to Houthi attacks on Saudi oil tankers; Houthis vowed to escalate
Oil prices exceeded $100 per barrel for first time since May; Australia reassured citizens about fuel supply security
